experiences.name: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore the stunning La Jolla Cove with the family, snorkeling among colorful fish and sea lions in the protected marine reserve. The calm, clear waters are perfect for kids, and the surrounding beach offers tide pools to discover crabs, starfish, and anemones. Rent snorkel gear nearby or bring your own for a budget-friendly adventure.

experiences.name: San Diego Zoo Visit
experiences.description: One of the world's most famous zoos, the San Diego Zoo is home to over 3,500 animals across 650 species. Kids and adults alike will love seeing giant pandas, koalas, giraffes, and polar bears. The guided bus tour and aerial tram provide easy ways to cover the expansive grounds while learning from expert guides.

experiences.name: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic
experiences.description: Head to the iconic Coronado Beach, consistently rated one of the best beaches in the USA, for a relaxed family afternoon and sunset picnic. Build sandcastles, splash in the gentle waves, and watch the sun dip behind the Hotel del Coronado. Pick up fresh tacos and snacks from local food trucks near the ferry landing to keep costs low.

experiences.name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park Exploration
experiences.description: Step back in time at California's birthplace, where adobe buildings, costumed docents, and free museums bring 19th-century Mexican and early American life to vivid reality. Enjoy free entry to most exhibits, browse colorful artisan shops, and treat the family to authentic street tacos and churros from the lively food stalls. A fantastic cultural experience that won't break the budget.
experiences.location: Old Town State Historic Park, Old Town San Diego

experiences.name: Mission Bay Kayaking and Bike Ride

Afterward, rent bikes and cruise the scenic Mission Bay Bike Path along the waterfront, stopping at Fiesta Island for open green space and bay views. A full day of active outdoor fun at an affordable price.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at San Diego Airport at 12:00 PM via flight WN. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (take the MTS Bus Route 992 or a rideshare to save money), and check in to Mission Bay Family Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk or bike ride to Mission Bay Park — just steps from the resort. Let the kids splash in the calm bay waters, explore the grassy picnic areas, and enjoy the stunning views. Rent a paddleboat or kayak from the park's rental stand (approx. $15–$20/hour) for a fun, affordable family activity.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Mission Boulevard for a casual evening. Visit Belmont Park, a free-to-enter beachfront amusement park with a historic wooden roller coaster and arcade games (pay only for rides you choose). Enjoy the lively boardwalk atmosphere as the sun sets over Mission Beach.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — look for grab-and-go options under $10.
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable tacos at Rigoberto's Taco Shop near Mission Bay (~$8–$12 per person) — a San Diego staple for budget-friendly, authentic Mexican food.
meals.dinner: Head to World Famous restaurant on Ocean Front Walk for casual fish tacos and burgers with ocean views. Budget-friendly options available for ~$12–$18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light since you arrive at noon. Focus on getting settled, resting, and orienting yourselves around Mission Bay. Pick up groceries at a nearby Vons or Ralphs supermarket for snacks and breakfast items to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early with a visit to La Jolla Cove for snorkeling and a beach day. Arrive by 9:00 AM to snag free parking and beat the crowds. Rent snorkel gear nearby (~$10–$15) or bring your own. Swim among colorful fish, garibaldi, and friendly sea lions in the crystal-clear protected waters of the cove. The kids will love it!
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, walk along the La Jolla Cove trail to Children's Pool and Seal Rock to spot harbor seals lounging on the beach — completely free! Then explore the charming La Jolla Village for window shopping and people-watching. Visit the free outdoor exhibits at the Birch Aquarium's tide pools (tide pool access is free; aquarium entry is ~$20/adult, $14/child if you choose to go inside).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mission Bay area and enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach. Build sandcastles, play beach volleyball, or simply watch the sunset over the Pacific from Mission Beach boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Eat in — use groceries from your hotel room for a simple breakfast (cereal, fruit, yogurt) to save money.
meals.lunch: Pack a cooler lunch from your hotel or grab affordable burritos from a local taqueria in La Jolla Village (~$8–$10 per person). Try Vallarta Express for a budget-friendly option.
meals.dinner: Pick up fresh fish tacos and ceviche at Rubio's Coastal Grill near Mission Bay (~$10–$14 per person) — a San Diego original and family favorite.

day_by_day.notes: La Jolla Cove is about 15 miles from Mission Bay Resort. Drive or use Uber/Lyft (approx. $20–$25 each way). Parking at La Jolla Cove is free on street but fills up fast — arrive early! Bring sunscreen, water shoes, and towels. Water temperature in August is typically a comfortable 68–72°F.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Old Town San Diego State Historic Park — California's birthplace and a completely FREE attraction! Explore adobe buildings, watch costumed docents demonstrate 1800s life, and visit the free museums including the Whaley House Museum grounds and the free historic exhibits. Kids love the hands-on history and the colorful Mexican marketplace atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Old Town, head to Balboa Park — one of the greatest free urban parks in the country. Walk the beautiful Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, explore the free outdoor gardens (Japanese Friendship Garden, Rose Garden, Desert Garden), and take advantage of free museum Tuesdays (several Balboa Park museums offer free admission to San Diego residents on rotating Tuesdays — check which ones apply). The park's central fountain and plazas are perfect for a family picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mission Bay for a sunset kayak or paddleboard session. Many rental spots along Mission Bay offer evening rates. Alternatively, enjoy a bonfire on the beach (fire rings available at Mission Beach — free!) and roast marshmallows as a family.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast burritos from a local café or eat in at the hotel. Try Café on Park near Balboa Park for ~$8–$12 per person.
meals.lunch: Eat at Old Town's free picnic areas with a packed lunch, or try the affordable Mexican food at Casa de Reyes in Old Town (~$10–$15 per person for tacos and enchiladas).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple dinner using your hotel's amenities or nearby grocery items, or grab affordable pizza from Woodstock's Pizza near Mission Beach (~$15–$20 for a shareable pizza).

day_by_day.notes: Old Town San Diego is about 6 miles from Mission Bay — a short 10-minute drive or take MTS Bus Route 8. Balboa Park is another 3 miles from Old Town. Both are easily combined into one day trip. Wear comfortable walking shoes as both sites involve significant walking on uneven surfaces.

day_by_day.morning: Take the 15-minute ferry from Broadway Pier in downtown San Diego to Coronado Island (~$5.50 per person each way — a budget-friendly and scenic ride!). Arrive at Coronado and walk or rent bikes (~$10/hour) along the beautiful Coronado Beach strand. Consistently rated one of America's best beaches, Coronado Beach features wide white sand, gentle waves, and stunning views of the Hotel del Coronado.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a full afternoon on Coronado Beach. Build sandcastles, bodysurf the gentle waves, and explore the historic Hotel del Coronado grounds (free to walk around outside). The kids can play in the surf while parents relax on the gorgeous shoreline. Explore Orange Avenue, Coronado's charming main street, for window shopping and a cold treat.
day_by_day.evening: Set up a sunset picnic on Coronado Beach — one of the most magical sunsets in all of San Diego. Watch the sun dip below the Pacific horizon with the iconic Hotel del Coronado as your backdrop. Take the ferry back to downtown afterward and enjoy a short evening stroll along the waterfront Embarcadero before heading back to Mission Bay.

meals.breakfast: Eat in at the hotel or grab pastries and coffee from a local bakery near Mission Bay before heading to the ferry.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on Coronado Beach — buy supplies at a Vons or Ralphs the night before. Think sandwiches, fruit, chips, and drinks (~$5–$8 per person).
meals.dinner: Try Clayton's Coffee Shop on Orange Avenue in Coronado — a beloved local diner with hearty, affordable meals (~$12–$16 per person). Or head back to Mission Bay and grab fish and chips at a casual spot along the boardwalk.

day_by_day.notes: The Coronado Ferry departs from Broadway Pier in downtown San Diego. Parking downtown can be expensive — consider taking an Uber/Lyft to the pier or using the MTS Trolley to the Santa Fe Depot stop (a short walk to the pier). The ferry runs every 30–60 minutes. Coronado Beach can get crowded on weekends — a Monday or Tuesday visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning back at Mission Bay, enjoying the resort's amenities and the beautiful bay one last time. Take an early morning walk along the 27-mile Mission Bay Park path, enjoy a final swim, or rent a surrey bike for the whole family (~$25–$35/hour) for a fun last-day activity along the boardwalk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free outdoor exhibits at the USS Midway Museum exterior along the Embarcadero (or splurge on the full museum entry at ~$26/adult, $18/child if budget allows — it's one of San Diego's top family attractions). Alternatively, explore Seaport Village, a free waterfront shopping and dining complex with beautiful bay views, street performers, and a historic carousel (~$3/ride).
day_by_day.evening: Wrap up your San Diego trip with a final dinner at a local favorite. Pack up your belongings, check out of Mission Bay Family Resort, and head to the airport for your departure flight. Reflect on five amazing days of beaches, history, and family fun in America's Finest City!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast using remaining groceries, or treat the family to a sit-down breakfast at Broken Yolk Café — a San Diego institution with generous portions (~$10–$14 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab affordable street tacos or burritos from a food truck along the Embarcadero or Seaport Village (~$8–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Enjoy a farewell dinner at Hodad's in Ocean Beach or downtown — famous for massive, affordable burgers in a fun, casual atmosphere (~$12–$16 per person). A perfect budget-friendly San Diego send-off!

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan accordingly — San Diego International Airport (SAN) is only about 10–15 minutes from Mission Bay. Factor in check-out time (typically 11:00 AM) and allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport procedures. Consider storing luggage at the hotel after checkout if your flight is in the evening.

experiences.description: Rent kayaks or pedal boats and explore the calm, sheltered waters of Mission Bay, a 4,200-acre aquatic park perfect for families. Afterward, rent bikes and cruise the scenic Mission Bay Bike Path along the waterfront, stopping at Fiesta Island for open green space and bay views. A full day of active outdoor fun at an affordable price.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight WN lands at 12:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (rideshare or rental car ~30 min), and check in early at Mission Bay Family Resort. Drop off bags, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort map and amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mission Bay Kayaking and Bike Ride: Since the resort sits right on Mission Bay, head straight to the water after settling in. Rent kayaks or pedal boats from the resort's waterfront or a nearby outfitter (e.g., Mission Bay Sportcenter). Paddle the calm, sheltered 4,200-acre bay, spot pelicans and sailboats, and let the kids burn off travel energy. Alternatively, rent bikes and cruise the scenic 27-mile Mission Bay path.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Mission Bay boardwalk at sunset for a relaxed first evening. Explore the resort grounds, let kids play at the beach, and enjoy the laid-back San Diego vibe before an early dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport before landing or pick up snacks at a convenience store near the resort.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, casual bite near the resort — try Catamaran Resort's Oceana Coastal Kitchen or pick up sandwiches from a nearby deli like Submarina to eat bayside.
meals.dinner: Firefly Eatery & Bar (Mission Bay area) — family-friendly, mid-range American fare with waterfront views. Expect $15–$25 per adult entrée.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you're arriving at noon. Prioritize comfort and proximity to the hotel. Pre-book kayak rentals online if possible. Mission Bay is extremely calm and safe for young children.

day_by_day.morning: San Diego Zoo Visit: Head to Balboa Park for a full morning at one of the world's most famous zoos. Arrive at opening (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the August heat. Highlights include the Giant Panda exhibit, African Savanna, and the Skyfari aerial tram. Purchase tickets online in advance to save time ($67 adults / $57 children, mid-range budget tip: skip the add-on packages).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the San Diego Zoo — spend the full afternoon covering the Elephant Odyssey, Reptile House, and the Children's Zoo area. Grab lunch inside the zoo at Albert's Restaurant or one of the mid-range food stands (budget ~$15–$20 per person). Plan to leave around 4:00–4:30 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mission Bay for a relaxing evening swim at the resort beach. Kids can play in the sand while parents unwind. Enjoy a casual dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort restaurant or a nearby spot like The Broken Yolk Cafe (Mission Bay area) — hearty American breakfast, ~$12–$18 per person.
meals.lunch: Albert's Restaurant inside the San Diego Zoo — sit-down mid-range dining with a nice garden setting. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Rubio's Coastal Grill (multiple locations near Mission Bay) — casual, family-friendly fish tacos and burritos, ~$10–$15 per person. A San Diego staple.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen — the zoo involves 3–5 miles of walking. Arrive early to see the most active animals before midday heat. August temperatures in San Diego average 72–78°F with low humidity.

day_by_day.morning: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day: Drive ~15 minutes north to the stunning La Jolla Cove. Arrive by 9:00 AM for the clearest water and calmest surf. Rent snorkel gear from La Jolla Cove Snorkel & Scuba (on-site, ~$20–$30/person) and explore the underwater ecological reserve — kids and adults will love spotting colorful fish, garibaldi (California's state fish), and curious sea lions lounging on the rocks. The cove is protected and ideal for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, walk north along the La Jolla coastline to Children's Pool Beach to watch harbor seals up close. Then explore the charming La Jolla Village — browse boutique shops, pop into the Birch Aquarium at Scripps (great for kids, ~$22 adults / $16 children), and enjoy the scenic coastal bluffs. Head back to the hotel by 5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort pool or Mission Bay beach. Optional: catch the sunset from the resort's waterfront — August sunsets over the bay are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee from Pannikin Coffee & Tea in La Jolla Village before heading to the cove — a beloved local café.
meals.lunch: The Cottage La Jolla — a beloved brunch and lunch spot in La Jolla Village. Expect $14–$22 per person for sandwiches, salads, and fresh seafood options.
meals.dinner: Peohe's or Miguel's Cocina on Coronado (if driving) — OR stay local and try World Famous Restaurant on Mission Beach for fresh seafood with ocean views, ~$18–$28 per entrée.

day_by_day.notes: La Jolla Cove can get crowded by 10:30 AM on weekdays in summer — arriving early is key. Water visibility is best in the morning. Bring water shoes as the rocky entry can be slippery. Parking is free along Coast Blvd but fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park Exploration: Drive ~10 minutes to California's birthplace for a free, immersive history experience. Walk through adobe buildings, watch costumed docents demonstrate 1800s crafts, and explore free museums including the Whaley House Museum (America's most haunted house, ~$10/person). Kids love the hands-on demonstrations and the colorful Mexican marketplace atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic Prep + Afternoon at Coronado: Take the scenic Coronado Bridge (~10 min drive) to Coronado Island. Spend the afternoon on Coronado Beach — consistently ranked one of America's best beaches with wide, powdery white sand and gentle waves. Build sandcastles, swim, and relax. Walk along the iconic Hotel del Coronado (free to explore the exterior and grounds) and browse the Coronado Ferry Landing shops.
day_by_day.evening: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic: Stay on Coronado Beach for the famous sunset. Pick up a picnic spread from the Coronado Ferry Landing Marketplace or a nearby grocery store — grab charcuterie, fresh fruit, local cheeses, and sparkling lemonade. Spread out a blanket and watch the sky turn pink and orange over the Pacific. A magical, budget-friendly family evening.

meals.breakfast: Café Coyote in Old Town San Diego — lively, colorful Mexican breakfast spot with fresh tortillas made tableside. ~$12–$18 per person.
meals.lunch: Old Town Mexican Café (Old Town) — a local institution famous for carnitas and handmade tortillas. ~$12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: DIY Sunset Picnic on Coronado Beach — pick up supplies from Coronado Ferry Landing Marketplace or Vons Grocery on Orange Ave. Budget ~$15–$20 per person for a relaxed, memorable beachside meal.

day_by_day.notes: Old Town is entirely free to explore (some museum admissions are nominal). Coronado Beach parking is free along Ocean Blvd. The Coronado Bridge offers stunning views — consider the Coronado Ferry ($5 each way) for a fun alternative to driving. Bring a light jacket for the evening — coastal breezes pick up after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Mission Bay: Enjoy a slow, relaxed last morning at the resort. Take one final kayak paddle or bike ride along the Mission Bay path. Let the kids splash in the bay one last time. Pack souvenirs and take a family photo at the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — if afternoon/evening flight: Visit Balboa Park (free to walk the grounds, Spanish Colonial architecture, free outdoor concerts on Sundays) or revisit a favorite spot. If early departure: Check out of the resort, store luggage at the front desk, and grab a final San Diego meal before heading to the airport (SAN is ~15 min from Mission Bay).
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final evening in San Diego. If staying an extra evening, enjoy a farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant on Mission Beach boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — treat the family to the full resort breakfast buffet (if available) as a send-off, ~$15–$20 per person. OR try Hob Nob Hill, a classic San Diego diner since 1944, for pancakes and eggs (~$12–$16/person).
meals.lunch: Hodad's (Ocean Beach location, ~10 min from Mission Bay) — legendary San Diego burger joint, family-friendly with massive portions. ~$12–$16 per person. A must-try San Diego institution.
meals.dinner: If departing: grab a final bite at the airport. If staying: The Beachcomber at Crystal Pier (Pacific Beach) — casual seafood with stunning ocean pier views, ~$18–$28 per entrée.

day_by_day.notes: San Diego International Airport (SAN) is conveniently close — allow 20–30 minutes from Mission Bay plus standard TSA time (90 min recommended for domestic flights). Return any rental gear or bikes before checkout. Check resort late checkout options to maximize your final morning.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Mission Bay waterfront promenade. Enjoy the golden hour views over the bay before heading to dinner at a nearby waterfront restaurant.

meals.dinner: Firefly at Mission Bay: An upscale resort-adjacent restaurant offering wood-fired cuisine, premium steaks, and fresh Pacific seafood with stunning bay views. Ideal for a luxurious family welcome dinner.

day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the San Diego Zoo through the early afternoon, focusing on the Children's Zoo, African Rocks, and the Giant Panda habitat. Around 2:30 PM, transition to Balboa Park's surrounding gardens and museums for a leisurely cultural stroll before heading back to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the Mission Bay Family Resort's pool and spa facilities. Enjoy a private cabana booking with poolside service as the family winds down from a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast at the Mission Bay Family Resort's signature restaurant — enjoy a lavish buffet or à la carte options including fresh fruit, eggs Benedict, and artisan pastries overlooking the bay.
meals.lunch: Albert's Restaurant inside the San Diego Zoo: The zoo's premier dining destination offering California-inspired cuisine in a lush, treehouse-style setting surrounded by tropical plants. Enjoy gourmet salads, grilled entrees, and fresh-pressed juices.
meals.dinner: George's at the Cove (La Jolla): A legendary San Diego fine dining institution with sweeping ocean views. The rooftop Ocean Terrace offers a more casual yet upscale experience, while the main dining room delivers world-class California cuisine with an award-winning wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase San Diego Zoo tickets in advance online to skip general admission lines. The VIP Behind-the-Scenes Tour must be booked weeks ahead and is highly recommended for a luxury family experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the zoo spans 100 acres with significant terrain variation. Estimated drive from Mission Bay to the zoo is approximately 15 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day: Depart by 8:30 AM to beat the crowds at the stunning La Jolla Cove. The clear, calm waters make this ideal for families with children of all swimming levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, relax on the pristine La Jolla Cove beach with a private beach setup (umbrella, lounge chairs, and cooler arranged through a concierge beach service). Explore the surrounding La Jolla village — browse upscale boutiques, art galleries, and enjoy the dramatic coastal cliffs. Visit the Children's Pool area to observe harbor seals resting on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming La Jolla village at sunset before a world-class dinner. Walk along Prospect Street and admire the ocean panoramas as the sun dips below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — grab fresh pastries, yogurt parfaits, and coffee from the resort's grab-and-go café to enjoy en route.
meals.lunch: The Cottage La Jolla: A beloved La Jolla institution serving gourmet brunch and lunch in a charming cottage setting. Famous for their lemon ricotta pancakes, fresh seafood omelets, and garden patio dining.
meals.dinner: Herringbone La Jolla: A stunning, tree-lined fine dining experience in the heart of La Jolla village. Known for exceptional sustainable seafood, premium dry-aged steaks, and craft cocktails in a dramatic living-wall atmosphere. Perfect for a special family dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling tour at least 1–2 weeks in advance through a luxury outfitter such as Everyday California, which offers premium guided experiences. Bring water shoes, reef-safe sunscreen, and a change of dry clothes. La Jolla Cove parking fills quickly — arrange a private driver or rideshare for the day to avoid the hassle. Drive from Mission Bay is approximately 20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park Exploration: Travel back to California's birthplace with a morning visit to Old Town San Diego. Wander through beautifully preserved adobe buildings, interact with costumed docents, and explore free museums including the Whaley House and the Junipero Serra Museum. This immersive cultural experience is educational and engaging for the entire family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic Preparation & Afternoon: Cross the iconic Coronado Bridge to Coronado Island for an afternoon at one of America's most celebrated beaches. Arrange a luxury private beach picnic through a premium concierge service — complete with gourmet charcuterie, chilled champagne or sparkling lemonade for kids, plush blankets, and a private setup with a beach umbrella. Build sandcastles, swim in the gentle surf, and enjoy the white sand shores with the historic Hotel del Coronado as your backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic: Linger on Coronado Beach as the sun sets dramatically over the Pacific, painting the sky in brilliant oranges and pinks. This iconic setting with the illuminated Hotel del Coronado is truly magical. Cap the evening with a walk through the Hotel del Coronado's grand Victorian lobby and grounds.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort's waterfront restaurant — indulge in a full family breakfast with made-to-order omelets, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a premium pastry selection.
meals.lunch: Casa de Reyes in Old Town: An authentic, vibrant Mexican restaurant within Old Town's Fiesta de Reyes courtyard, serving traditional Mexican cuisine with premium margaritas and fresh guacamole prepared tableside.
meals.dinner: 1500 Ocean at Hotel del Coronado: An exquisite fine dining experience at the legendary Hotel del Coronado, featuring farm-to-table California cuisine with ocean-view terrace seating. An unforgettable setting to close a perfect beach day.

day_by_day.notes: The luxury beach picnic setup on Coronado Beach should be arranged 3–5 days in advance through a San Diego premium picnic company such as The Pop-Up Picnic Co. or similar concierge service. Old Town is approximately 10 minutes from Mission Bay; Coronado Beach is approximately 20–25 minutes via the Coronado Bridge. Consider hiring a private driver for the day for seamless transitions between locations.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Mission Bay for a leisurely final morning on the water. Rent a luxury electric boat or a premium stand-up paddleboard for a peaceful sunrise paddle around the bay. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's private beach and pool area for a relaxed, unhurried morning. Take time for a spa treatment at the resort spa — book couples or family massages to rejuvenate before the journey home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon shopping and exploration at Liberty Station, a beautifully redeveloped former Naval Training Center turned artisan marketplace in Point Loma — just 10 minutes from Mission Bay. Browse local boutiques, art galleries, and specialty shops for premium San Diego souvenirs. Visit the Public Market for locally made goods, gourmet foods, and artisan products.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner at a premier San Diego restaurant before packing and preparing for departure. Reflect on an extraordinary family trip over a world-class meal.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final resort breakfast — order the full à la carte experience with lobster eggs Benedict, fresh açaí bowls, smoked salmon platters, and premium coffee drinks. Savor the bay views one last time.
meals.lunch: Stone Brewing World Bistro & Gardens at Liberty Station: A stunning craft beer garden and gourmet restaurant with lush outdoor gardens, farm-to-table cuisine, and an exceptional selection of craft beverages. Family-friendly with an elevated, relaxed atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Addison at Fairmont Grand Del Mar (or downtown alternative: Juniper & Ivy): San Diego's only Michelin two-starred restaurant, Addison offers an extraordinary tasting menu experience with impeccable service — the ultimate luxury farewell dinner. For a more family-casual luxury option, Juniper & Ivy in Little Italy offers inventive California cuisine in a stunning converted warehouse space.

day_by_day.notes: Addison at Fairmont Grand Del Mar requires reservations made well in advance (often 4–6 weeks) and is approximately 30 minutes from Mission Bay — arrange a private car service for the evening. Check-out from the resort should be coordinated with the concierge; request a late checkout if the return flight is in the evening. Ensure all luggage and departure logistics are arranged the night before for a stress-free final day.
